title: Social media content of idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis groups and pages on facebook: Cross-sectional analysis
screen_reason: Reports the share of a systematically sampled set of Facebook posts that contained potentially harmful information, i.e. therapy recommendations contrary to IPF clinical practice guidelines, with an explicit denominator (523 posts from 39 groups and pages) and a second share at the group/page level. The guideline-concordance judgement is an external ground truth applied to specific claims, which the protocol treats as CONTENT rather than QUALITY.

estimates.country: Not stated (English-language, publicly available Facebook groups and pages; authors based in Canada, Switzerland and the United States)
estimates.platform: Facebook groups and pages focused on idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis
estimates.date: Search executed on a single date, January 4, 2019; sampled posts had a median age of 630 days (IQR 259-1381, range 0-4271), so the content itself spans roughly 2007-2019
estimates.measure_type: % of sampled Facebook posts in IPF groups and pages that contained potentially harmful information (a therapy recommendation contrary to IPF guidelines)
estimates.value_raw: 5% contained potentially harmful information (of 523 posts analysed)
estimates.denominator: 523 posts, being every 10th post from the 12 groups and 27 pages meeting eligibility criteria (220 posts from groups, 303 from pages)
estimates.definition: Post coded as containing potentially harmful information if it recommended pharmacologic or nonpharmacologic therapies not recommended by current IPF clinical practice guidelines (examples given: stem cell transplant, specific dietary modifications).
estimates.misinfo_def: "Posts were considered harmful if they recommended pharmacologic or nonpharmacologic therapies (eg, stem cell transplant, specific dietary modifications) not recommended by current IPF guidelines" - the paper calls this misinformation in its conclusion ('posts with misinformation and less guideline content have higher user engagement').
estimates.source_quote: Of these, 42% contained guideline content, 24% provided useful support, 20% provided useful scientific information, and 5% contained potentially harmful information.
estimates.page_loc: Abstract, Results; the same figure appears in the Results section under 'Harmful Post Content' and in the Discussion
estimates.ground_truth_detail: Two authors independently coded every sampled post in duplicate against the ATS/ERS/JRS/ALAT clinical practice guidelines for the diagnosis and treatment of IPF; unweighted kappa was used for every variable with an acceptability cut-off of 0.70, and a third independent author arbitrated whenever kappa fell below 0.70. The kappa values themselves are not reported in the text, only the threshold and the arbitration rule.
estimates.moderator_quote: The terms "IPF" and "idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis" were separately entered in Facebook's search function on January 4, 2019 to identify IPF-related groups and pages.
estimates.notes: Coded CONTENT rather than QUALITY because the harmful-content label is a truth/appropriateness judgement against an external ground truth (the ATS/ERS/JRS/ALAT guidelines) applied to a specific claim - a recommendation for a therapy the guidelines do not recommend - so a wholly accurate post cannot pick up the label. That is the protocol's stated CONTENT test ('guideline concordance stated as accurate/inaccurate'). The paper's OTHER instrument, the 0-30 guideline content score, is a completeness measure and is QUALITY: a post can score 0 simply by being short and still be entirely true. It is reported only as means, so it generates no row in any case. breadth coded misleading rather than false because 'not recommended by current guidelines' includes unproven as well as disproven therapies.

estimates.notes: A second denominator for the same coding: the share of communities carrying any misinformation, rather than the share of posts. Not a definition variant (the numerator definition is identical) but it must not be pooled with row 0 - it is the same 523 posts aggregated to their 39 host groups/pages. Confidence medium because no count is given (35% of 39 falls between 13 and 14 groups/pages, and the Discussion rounds it to 'one third'), and because the every-10th-post sampling means a group with harmful posts could be missed, so this is a lower bound. The source quote begins mid-sentence: the preceding clause, 'Only 5% of the posts contained potentially harmful information,', sits on a different physical line of the two-column PDF rendering and is not contiguous with it in the text file.

missed_or_uncertain: (1) The 0-30 guideline content score is the paper's main instrument and is QUALITY, not prevalence: it counts how many of 30 prespecified guideline-supported content items a post covers, so a truthful post scores low simply by being brief. It is reported only as means by source and focus (e.g. guideline-focused posts 11.2 (10.0), non-IPF posts 0.1 (0.3)), i.e. no share of items, so under the protocol it yields no row at all. (2) '42% contained guideline content' is the share of posts containing ANY guideline-recommended content - the complement of a content score of zero. It is a presence-of-useful-information share, not a misinformation share, and its complement (58% with no guideline content) would be a computed complement barred by R8, so no row. (3) '24% provided useful support' and '20% provided useful scientific information' are likewise usefulness shares, not veracity. (4) Post source shares (nonmedical users 445/523, 85.1%; foundations or medical organizations 53/523, 10.1%; industry 24/523, 4.6%; medical professionals 1/523, 0.2%) and post focus shares (news 152, 29.1%; other IPF 131, 25.0%; non-IPF 81, 15.5%; advice 80, 15.3%; advertisement 65, 12.4%; opinion 7, 1.3%; guidelines 5, 1.0%; insurance 2, 0.4%) are attributions and topics, not veracity. (5) The regression results (Tables 2-3, Table S4) are associations between harmful content and engagement, not prevalence. (6) The reported kappa values are not given, only the 0.70 acceptability cut-off and the third-author arbitration rule, so inter-rater reliability cannot be appraised. (7) No country is stated anywhere: the frame is English-language public Facebook groups and pages, hence country_norm Global. (8) Sampling every 10th post is a systematic rather than random sample and the authors note it reduced their coverage of rare sources and may have missed rarely discussed harmful interventions, so 5% is best read as a lower bound. (9) Multimedia Appendix 1 (Tables S1-S4, Figure S1) is not in the text file, so the harmful-content regression detail and the list of nonrecommended therapies could not be checked.

rob.design: Cross-sectional content analysis. Frame: Facebook's own search function queried on a single date (January 4, 2019) from a fresh account with cleared history and cookies, for 'IPF' and 'idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis' separately, yielding 126 groups and 191 pages; exclusions were non-English, closed/private groups, non-IPF focus and duplicates, leaving 12 groups and 27 pages. Every 10th post was sampled, giving 523 posts (220 from groups, 303 from pages). Two authors independently coded each group, page and post in duplicate against 30 prespecified guideline-supported content items and against a harmful-content definition drawn from the ATS/ERS/JRS/ALAT guidelines; unweighted kappa with a 0.70 cut-off and a third author arbitrating below it (kappa values not reported). Analysis clustered by group/page with a sandwich estimator. Limitations acknowledged by the authors: systematic every-10th-post sampling under-covers rare post sources and may miss rarely discussed harmful interventions; closed groups and non-English content excluded; only IPF-focused (not broader ILD) communities included. No country, no denominator of platform users, and no reliability statistic are reported.
rob.item6_quote: Posts were considered harmful if they recommended pharmacologic or nonpharmacologic therapies (eg, stem cell transplant, specific dietary modifications) not recommended by current IPF guidelines
rob.item10_quote: Eligibility criteria were met by 12 groups and 27 pages, leading to analysis of 523 posts. Of these, 42% contained guideline content, 24% provided useful support, 20% provided useful scientific information, and 5% contained potentially harmful information.
